narrative.origin_story: Aïssatou Diop is 36 and runs a four-person climate-fintech in Dakar.
narrative.manifesto:
The market calls some places "frontier" because it has not yet learned to see them.

In Dakar, a climate-fintech founder is rebuilding insurance for smallholder farmers using satellite data and a mobile-money rail. In São Paulo's Brasilândia, a young architect is designing modular school infrastructure that ships in 60 days. In Karachi, a doctor and an engineer are building rural diagnostic kits that cost a tenth of what an equivalent kit costs in São Paulo. Each of these founders has built more, with less, in less time, than most ventures in the cities the world calls central.

The market does not see them because the market's pattern recognition is built on resumes, conferences, accelerators, and second-degree connections that all converge on the same three cities. Capital follows the pattern. The pattern misses the founder.

Cacti operates inside that miss.

We are a fund — disciplined about thesis, allocation, governance, and exit. We deploy patient capital at $100K to $2M check sizes against ventures in hidden frontiers. We co-invest with local capital wherever it exists. We publish our investment thesis. We publish the portfolio. We publish the governance. We publish the rejection rate.

We do not romanticize scarcity. We do not call founders "beneficiaries." We do not subsidize storytelling. We invest because we believe these founders are the next decade's outliers, and the market will eventually agree.

When it does, we will already be in the cap table.

This is impact with the manners of an institution. This is dignity that lives in structure, not in a campaign.
